caption:
A brief is only as good as what happens when someone checks it later. That is the standard we build to — not persuasion, verification.

Every alert carries a confidence grade: confirmed, assessed, or unknown. Every call is logged against the imagery pass that produced it. Nothing is rounded up to sound more certain than the evidence supports.

This matters past the first decision cycle. If a response gets contested — in a briefing, in a review, in a courtroom — the record has to hold up on its own, not on the reputation of whoever wrote it. That is the only kind of intelligence worth paying for.

In the Numan flood hindcast, the reach-monitoring array flagged the signature four days ahead of the official warning. In the 2021 control year, it stayed quiet, correctly. We publish both outcomes, not just the one that looks good.
